title: Negative-Control Bias Bounds and Honest Width under Weak Factor Confounding
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field and NOT salvageable in scope; paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < 7.4.
gap_reasons: The note proves a matched class-wide honest-width elbow for the centered, single-control endpoint in a fixed-dimensional Gaussian experiment with known noise and orientation.
Its pointwise width result covers control-variance floors at least as large as sampling resolution; below that scale, the proof gives a class-wide bound rather than a pointwise frontier.

The broader joint bias region receives a fourth-root Hausdorff estimation rate, but no honest joint-region inference theorem, so the delivered inference result is narrower than the project's joint-region aim.
The narrow sampling model and lack of a worked application or computational evidence constrain its projected leading-journal score.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived exact PSD/nuclear-support geometry, a fourth-root Hausdorff frontier on a regular Gaussian subclass, a positive-rank negative-control instability witness, and a sharp class-wide control-strength honest-width elbow; the math panel passed with no findings. The field-tier claim collapsed because upper attainment remained confined to a fixed-dimensional known-noise, known-orientation, single-control subexperiment, while all-floor pointwise matching and honest inference for the full joint region were not delivered. Reaching field tier would require a newly anchored all-regime pointwise inference program, broader unknown-orientation or multiple-control theory, and application evidence rather than a bounded repair.
tldr: For a centered exact negative control in the known-noise Gaussian factor subexperiment, the sharp causal-bias endpoint is a Schur-complement support. Its local modulus depends on both residual variance and target-control alignment. A positive-rank covariance pair and a finitely honest projected interval establish the class-wide control-strength elbow \(\kappa\sqrt{t_n/(\gamma+t_n)}\), with \(t_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\). The same interval attains the pointwise local expected-width order once \(\gamma\ge t_n\); below that scale, uniform honest width remains of constant order. Whole-region fourth-root uncertainty, coordinate versus joint separation, and positive-rank factor-selection loss support the central result.
gap: Kang et al. give population negative-control geometry, while Cox and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye provide weak-identification and projection coverage frameworks. The covariance-to-centered-exact-control support modulus and its matching honest expected-width frontier have not been established by the inspected theorem texts.
fill: Establish a two-dimensional one-control Schur perturbation frontier over an explicit positive variance floor, prove a Gaussian two-point expected-width lower bound, and show a finite-sample honest covariance-projection interval attains the corresponding unconditional expected-width rate on a logarithmic-floor subclass.
